header: One mast, four sensors, twelve years of readings
bodytext:
A Marnau station is deliberately dull. A galvanised mast in the bank, a sealed logger box, four probes on a cable, and a solar panel that has to survive a winter under willow shade. Nothing on it is bespoke, because a part that cannot be replaced from a van on a Tuesday is a part that eventually stops the series.

Every station sends its readings over the mobile network every fifteen minutes and keeps a local copy for ninety days. When a mast goes silent — and each winter two or three do — the gap is filled from that copy on the next site visit rather than interpolated.
caption: Station 14 after the spring service, before the probes go back in.
